# Normal distribution {#sec-normal}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

## Formal {.unnumbered}

$$
f(x) = \frac{1}{\sigma \sqrt{2\pi}}
       \exp\left(
         -\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}
       \right)
$${#eq-normal}

## Examples {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Normal Distribution - Probability Density Function with different means and standard deviations"
#| label: fig-normal-dist

# Set up the plot with appropriate range
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-6, 8), ylim = c(0, 0.4),
     xlab = "x", ylab = "f(x)",
     main = "Normal Distribution - Probability Density Function")

# Define parameters and colors
params <- list(
  list(mean = 0, sd = 1, label = "μ=0, σ=1", color = "blue"),
  list(mean = 0, sd = 2, label = "μ=0, σ=2", color = "red"),
  list(mean = 3, sd = 2, label = "μ=3, σ=2", color = "green")
)

# Plot each distribution
for (i in seq_along(params)) {
  mean_val <- params[[i]]$mean
  sd_val <- params[[i]]$sd
  color <- params[[i]]$color

  # Create sequence of x values
  x <- seq(-6, 8, length.out = 500)
  y <- dnorm(x, mean = mean_val, sd = sd_val)

  # Plot the curve
  lines(x, y, col = color, lwd = 2)
}

# Add legend
legend("topright",
       legend = c("μ=0, σ=1", "μ=0, σ=2", "μ=3, σ=2"),
       col = c("blue", "red", "green"),
       lwd = 2,
       cex = 0.9)

# Add grid for better readability
grid()
```
